argument.native_question: The exact Kapanga key and three Luiza keys have the native interior kind for original AGO ADM1 Lunda Norte, feature ordinal 11, negative ordinal 0. Kapanga’s Lunda Sul, Cambulo, Muconda, and Saurimo operands and Luiza’s Cambulo operand have empty kinds. Each target’s full distinct negative list remains preserved; no other province or municipality is silently substituted.
argument.historical_rule: The actual Jentgen and IBS144 readings distinguish the Kasai–Luao river boundary from the Kwango–Kasai pillar series and the southern watershed. The Kasai thalweg provision and its 1910 correction cannot be replaced by a general pillar-to-pillar line. Tshitatu 4 October 1922, Kwilu 1 March 1923, and Kwango–Utungila 20 and 30 June 1923 are separate records. The 34-pillar table is not a set of universal controls for these upstream river cells; Jentgen’s drainage corrections described as ad referendum are not treated as adopted modern changes.
argument.source_construction: The original Lunda Norte native feature and geometry are pinned. The exact AGO ADM1 source archive remains unread; the known Census processing history is a comparator and cannot establish Lunda Norte’s exact sourceData relation or local edge change. COD’s frozen target/source and physical rows are preserved. Neither a land mask nor an archive label provides a surveyed river position.
argument.mismatch_assessment: The specific native interior exclusion survives the legal and survey context. The executed research has not tied either export’s disputed edge to a contemporaneous thalweg, a usable survey control, or a verified modern transformation. No side assignment or source-error conclusion follows. The four centers’ presence in a catalogue bounding box establishes relevance only.
argument.reasonable_failed_qualification: Actual Jentgen pages 75–76 and the cited IBS144 passages were read. Their original-record identities were pursued in the official Cartothèque catalogue and AfricaMuseum record 004579. That record identifies a relevant 1924 Pereira/Weber Kasai survey map; its actual 497×682 preview was obtained and viewed but does not resolve fine labels or controls. The record lists hardcopy distribution and no linked full digital resource. The direct footnote gives Ministry of Colonies archives, not a retrievable journal volume or page. Exact AGO ADM1 retrieval remains restricted; the bounded local lookup did not recover its ZIP.
argument.proposal_basis: These four cells are submitted as a separate researched-unresolved proposal on the cumulative river-boundary, survey-record, actual preview, and source-lineage investigation. The specific remaining map/minutes opportunity is material and disclosed. This proposal does not assert that human-mediated custody retrieval was attempted, failed, or exhausted. Independent assessment must decide whether completed substantive work and this actual operating limit satisfy the original unresolved contract; this worker does not pre-accept them.
argument.remaining_finite_step: Obtain a readable copy or consult AfricaMuseum BE-RMCA-EARTHS-004579, checking its graticule, survey conventions, and relation to Tshitatu 4 October 1922. State Archives portfolio 111/card 2, old 287, and related Kasai survey records are specific alternative custody leads. Original signed minutes and the 30 June 1923 table remain unread. No custodian correspondence or appointment action is authorized or performed.
argument.scope_exclusions: The Noqui–Kwango 1913 text, Cabinda controls, and the separate southern watershed date discrepancy do not clear these Kasai cells. No universal requirement for every original is imposed, but the identified directly relevant map opportunity is not hidden.

metadata_fields_read.idCredit:
CENSUS DATA

Age-Sex data: Resultados Definitivos do Recenseamento Geral da População e Habitação de Angola 2014, Quadro 1.04: População Residente por Grupos Etários e Municípios, Segundo a Área de Residência, Sexo e Índice de Masculinidade. Instituto Nacional de Estatística de Angola. Available online at https://www.ine.gov.ao/publicacoes/populacao-e-sociedade/ (provincial reports must be downloaded individually, accessed September 5, 2019). The U.S. Census Bureau cannot guarantee the accuracy of non-U.S. census and survey data.

GEOSPATIAL BOUNDARIES

International boundaries coincide with the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset from the U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. Available online at http://geonode.state.gov (accessed 2019). Geospatial data for the first-order administrative divisions of Angola were downloaded from the Humanitarian Data Exchange, available online at http://data.humdata.org/dataset/angola-administrative-levels-0-3, "ago_admbnda_adm2_gadm_ine_ocha_20180904.zip" (accessed September 9, 2019). The U.S. Census Bureau cannot guarantee the accuracy of boundary placements.

NATIONAL ESTIMATES AND PROJECTIONS 

U.S. Census Bureau, Population Division.  INTERNATIONAL DATA BASE, September 2018 release, available at http://www.census.gov/data-tools/demo/idb/informationGateway.php, accessed in September 2019.

NATIONAL AND SUBNATIONAL AREA NAMES AND CODES 

(1) U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.  NGA GEOnet Names Server (GNS), available at http://geonames.nga.mil/gns/html/, accessed in September 2019.  For geographic area names from the U.S. Board on Geographic Names and the U.S. Government Federal Information Processing System (FIPS) codes.  
(2) U.S. Government Geopolitical Entities, Names, and Codes (GENC) Standard.  NSG Standards Registry, available at http://nsgreg.nga.mil/genc/discovery, accessed in August 2019.

metadata_fields_read.suppInfo:
SUBNATIONAL DIVISIONS

Angola's first-order administrative divisions: 18 provinces as of the 2014 census.

SHAPEFILES

The original shapefile downloaded by USCB staff had 161 polygons and matched the 2016 census districts (ADM2) after one minor change by USCB staff: In Lunda Norte province, Chitato district was split to accommodate the new Lóvua district. The U.S. Census Bureau aligned the boundaries in the shapefile to the “Large Scale International Boundary Line” (LSIB) polygon file (2018) from the U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. Then, the Census Bureau dissolved the LSIB-aligned shapefile into 18 polygons for Angola's first-order administrative divisions. The final shapefile contains 18 polygons, one for each of Angola's first-order administrative divisions (provinces) as reported by Instituto Nacional de Estatística de Angola in the 2014 census.

FEATURE AND ATTRIBUTE DETAILS

The 2000-2025 population estimates for Angola's administrative divisions are provided in the following 2 tables:
The Unicode tab-delimited text file (table) "Angola_5yr_age_sex_2000-2025_uscb_oct2019.txt," which can be joined to the shapefile via the common field "GEO_MATCH."
The Excel table "Angola_5yr_age_sex_2000-2025_508_uscb_oct2019.xlsx," formatted for accessibility in compliance with Section 508 of the U.S. Government's Federal Rehabilitation Act.

Details on processing of the census data and calculation of 2000-2025 estimates are provided in the "Census_Metadata" tab of the Excel file and "Methods for Calculating 5-Year Age Group Population Estimates by Sex for Subnational Areas" document.

For the subnational areas, the U.S. Board on Geographic Names (BGN) "approved" names from the NGA GEOnet Names Server (cited in the "Credits") were used.  For any area that a BGN name was not available, the name from the national census was used.  Official codes for the subnational areas from the country's national statistical office, when available, are entered in the "NSO_CODE" field in both the text and Excel tables.  Information on any alternative area names or recent name or boundary changes is entered in the "USCBCMNT" field.

A partial list of the fields in the Excel and Unicode text files, including all fields identifying geographic names and codes, is provided in the Excel file's "Data_Dictionary" tab.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

More detail on the U.S. Census Bureau subnational age and sex group estimates and maps for PEPFAR can be found in the document "Subnational Population Estimates Components for the Spatial Data Repository."  It includes a data dictionary that is similar to that in the Excel table.

ACCESS

The U.S. Census Bureau’s products for PEPFAR can be accessed from the SPATIAL DATA REPOSITORY: 

Zipped file containing geographic boundary data, tables with subnational population estimates, and instructions for linking (joining) the text file to the geographic boundary data: http://spatialdata.dhsprogram.com/home/.  This web address also provides access to data and maps from the DHS (Demographic and Health Surveys) Program.

Instructions for linking (joining) the text file to the geographic boundary data can also be found in a standalone methodology document in the Spatial Data Repository.

For more information, see the following methodology documents in the Spatial Data Repository:
(1) "Subnational Population Estimates Components for the Spatial Data Repository."
(2) "Methods for Calculating 5-Year Age Group Population Estimates by Sex for Subnational Areas." 

All of the above documents, tables, and geographic boundary data (zipped) are also available on the Census Bureau website at http://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/demo/international-programs/subnationalpopulation.html for download.

retained_crosswalk_result.method: Compare the pinned Lunda Norte polygon ring to the official 2019 Census Lunda Norte ring by ordered vertex sequence and bounds.
retained_crosswalk_result.result: All 1380 unique vertices of the pinned simplified ring match the 28897-unique-vertex Census ring in one reverse cyclic subsequence; closed endpoint and bounds match.
retained_crosswalk_result.assessment: Strong representation-level correspondence. Not proof that geoBoundaries inherited the 2019 feature attribution, and not a territorial-applicability or full-cell test.
